sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Common juniper is a highly variable evergreen conifer, ranging from a prostrate shrub to a tree about 10 m tall. It grows in heathland, pasture and open woodland across the Northern Hemisphere.

sections.title: Needles and cones
sections.text: Its sharp needles occur in whorls of three and have a pale band on the upper surface. Plants are usually male or female. The fleshy female cones take two or three years to ripen and turn blue-black; they are about 5–10 mm across.

sections.title: Uses and cautions
sections.text: The ripe cones, often called juniper berries, are used as a spice and to flavour some drinks. Concentrated preparations or large amounts may irritate the kidneys; the European Medicines Agency advises against medicinal use during pregnancy and in kidney disease.
